# palace-head-hashes-wrong fixture

Negative-test palace for `dreamball verify` invariant (e) — "timeline head-hashes
are leaves".

A valid `ball.*` palace whose `ball.timeline` lists, as a head-hash, the MINT
action — which is referenced as a `parent-hash` by the room-added action and is
therefore NOT a leaf. `dreamball verify` reports:

```
error: head-hash <fp> is not a leaf — it is referenced as parent by another action (invariant e)
```

The timeline's `head-hashes` are encoded with the CANONICAL shape —
`encodeTimeline` (`src/envelope_v2.zig`)'s repeated `[2]("head-hashes", bstr32)`
attribute pairs, one per hash — the same shape every other timeline in this
repo uses. (History: until Dreamball-mh0, this fixture deliberately hand-shaped
`head-hashes` as a single `["head-hashes", [bstr32, ...]]` pair — an ARRAY of
byte-strings — because `parseTimelineHeadHashes` only read that shape and
silently produced an empty head set on the real encoder's output. That made
this "negative" fixture pass for the wrong reason: it exercised the buggy
reader's own bug-compatible input, never the encoder `dreamball verify` sees
in production. `parseTimelineHeadHashes` (`src/cli/internal/verify.zig` and
its duplicate in `show.zig`) now reads the real repeated-attribute-pair shape,
and this fixture was regenerated straight from `encodeTimeline` — no more
hand-shaping. See Dreamball-mh0.)

Used by `scripts/cli-smoke.sh` (palace verify AC9).

## Regeneration

```bash
zig build export-palace-fixtures
```

Produced by `tools/export-palace-fixtures/main.zig` (`.head_not_leaf`
mutation). Do not hand-edit the CAS bytes — regenerate from the generator.
Note: `export-palace-fixtures` regenerates ALL 6 palace-* fixtures with fresh
ML-DSA-87/Ed25519 keys each run (by design — see the tool's header comment),
so running it will also touch the other 5 fixture directories even if their
structural shape is unaffected. When resolving Dreamball-mh0 only this
fixture's regenerated bytes were kept; the other 5 were reverted to avoid
unrelated churn.
